A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Sections 1–7, Appendices A–G, Figures 1–9 and Table 1 are available and can be matched despite reformatting and equation renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original trained-network experiments and numerical analyses, including sample-complexity measurements, neuron specialization, kernel propagation and attention experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Figures 2–3 and 5–9, with experimental settings documented in Appendices C, E and F.

M1.justification: The LDT-based variational approach, GP/GFL/specialization patterns and propagation rules are unchanged. The explicit CNN equation added in Appendix E.1.2 repeats the architecture already defined in Equation 78.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Gaussian Hermite/cubic regression, noisy parity classification, softmax-attention experiments and kernel-propagation tests using independent and power-law-correlated Gaussian inputs. No evaluated task or data scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same exact-LDT, heuristic and trained-network comparisons. No external comparison method is added or removed; newly cited related work is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Appendices C.5, E.3 and F retain the same model configurations, sample-size sweeps, ridge parameters and evaluation procedures, including the alignment threshold of 0.1 for estimating sample complexity in Figure 2.

E4.justification: The feature-amplification and normalization analyses in Figures 5–6, specialization analyses in Figures 2(c), 3(c), 7–8, and alignment-versus-MSE analysis in Figure 9 are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Appendix F retains the 300-network ensembles for two-layer and specialization analyses and the 30-network ensemble for Figure 3(a). Error-bar reporting is unchanged, with no added seed information, confidence intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 1's scaling expressions and the plotted results in Figures 2–3 and 5–9 are unchanged. Figure 2 adds missing d factors to the 42 and 24 legend labels, clarifying the linear dependence already shown by the curves and stated in both captions.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds a tolerance-based integral expression for near-unit alignment in footnote 2. The central bounds, variational derivations and appendix calculations otherwise remain unchanged; the repeated CNN equation does not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: v4 drops the introduction's explicit claim to re-derive Grokking transitions, retaining only the contextual specialization–Grokking connection. The central claims about predicting feature-learning patterns and sample-complexity scaling remain.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations and substantive limitations are retained. Section 7 still identifies general architectures, interacting features, learning dynamics and overfitting under mean-field scaling or vanishing ridge as unresolved issues.

D1.justification: The existing parametrizations, Langevin-training descriptions, numerical settings and outlier definitions remain documented in the same appendices. No new implementation, hardware, training-time or code/data-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The revised introduction newly cites Barbier et al. (2025), organizes prior Bayesian feature-learning mechanisms more explicitly and acknowledges theories for deeper architectures. The abstract removes its earlier restrictive characterization of existing theories as shallow or deep-linear.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten around a feature-learning taxonomy and two numbered contributions, while the derivation outline moves into Figure 1's caption. Terminology and local prose are edited, but the section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: v4 adopts conference typography and headers, expands Figure 1 with a rate-function node, corrects its alignment label and Figure 2's legends, compacts Table 1 and enlarges Figure 9. The figure inventory and underlying experimental displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The clearer introduction and derivation flowchart, corrected figure labels and repaired CNN cross-reference modestly improve readability. Removing the explicit Grokking-transition contribution claim and acknowledging deeper prior theories make the positioning more careful. The empirical evidence and substantive derivations remain essentially unchanged, so the improvement is limited.
